utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case number IT-98-29-T, the Prosecutor versus Stanislav Galic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. The Chamber still had to give a decision on the admissibility of document prenumbered D34, which, as we can see, is a UNPROFOR report. The document is admitted into evidence. It at least could have some relevance as to the intensity of fighting, firing, at the day -- at a day where the witness has testified that on the day of the incident he testified about that he did not hear any firing. At the same time, having admitted the document into evidence, the Chamber noted that while questioning the witness, Mr. Piletta-Zanin confronted the witness with the fact - or at least as he stated it as a fact from this document - that at least 120 shells were fired, and mortars. That's literally what he confronted the witness with, while the document says "approximately 120 mixed impact." Whether these are shells or mortars, that's, of course, a different issue. So despite the imprecision in confronting the witness with the content of the document, nevertheless we have some relevance, and of course this Chamber does not express itself on this moment on the probative value, the degree of probative value. Then I think the Prosecution could call its next witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. The next witness is Akif Mukanovic, and his evidence is relevant to scheduled sniping incident number 20.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ierace. Would you please bring the witness into the courtroom, Mr. Usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning. Can you hear me in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Welcome in this courtroom, Mr. Mukanovic. The Rules of Procedure and Evidence require you to make a solemn declaration prior to examination as a witness. The text of this declaration will be given to you by the usher, and I invite you to make that declaration now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please be seated, Mr. Mukanovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mukanovic, you will first be examined by Mr. Ierace or Mr. Mundis -- Mr. Ierace, of the Prosecution. The Prosecution has called you as a witness to The Hague. Please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Examined by Mr. Ierace:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, would you please give your full name for the record.

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Akif Mukanovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In 1992, were you living in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before the conflict broke out, what was your occupation?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: I was a maintenance man for the heating system.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was your address when the conflict broke out?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: During the conflict, it was the 27 Juli Obala 89, and later, the name of the street was changed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you live at that address throughout that conflict?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In 1992, who were the members of your immediate family?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: My wife, two children, and myself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Following -- at some stage following the outbreak of the conflict, did your occupation change?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: No. I don't know how you mean. Change how?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you become a member of the army?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Later on, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: In April 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you cease to be a member of the army?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: On the 1st of January, 1996.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the conflict, were you a member of the Bosnian government army known as the ABiH?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In January of 1994, who was living with you at your residence?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Myself, my wife, and our two children.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At that stage in January of 1994, how old were your children?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: My daughter was 17 at the time, and my son was 15 years old.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did your wife work?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had your wife ever worked apart from her household duties?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the nature of your residence? Was it a house, an apartment block, or something else?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: We lived in an apartment block which was four stories high, and we occupied the first floor. We lived in an apartment on the first floor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Approximately how far was your apartment block from the confrontation lines in January of 1994?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: About 800 metres as the crow flies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did any rooms of your apartment face the confrontation lines?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: My whole apartment and all the rooms in it were facing the front.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "facing the front," do you mean facing the confrontation lines, that is, the direction of the confrontation lines?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, the confrontation lines.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before January 1994, had there been any incidents during the armed conflict when bullets had entered your apartment?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that on one occasion or more than one occasion before January 1994?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: A number of occasions, many occasions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: By January 1994, had you and your family taken any steps to protect yourselves from fire into your apartment?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did those steps include taking measures to minimise opportunities for you and your family to be seen at night from the direction of the confrontation line?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What would you do at night, at night-time, in that regard?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: At night, we usually -- in addition to the blinds, we would put up blankets to make the rooms as dark as possible. So blinds and blankets.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said earlier that every room in your apartment faced the direction of the confrontation lines. Did those rooms include the kitchen?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the dining-room?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Indeed, did the dining-room have a window facing towards the direction of the confrontation lines?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you stood or sat in your dining-room and looked through the window, could you, in fact, by January 1994, see territory occupied by the VRS?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that you would put up a blanket or blankets at night to darken the rooms. Did that apply to the dining-room usually?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What other covering, if any, did you have on the dining-room window, typically, in January of 1994?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: We had a blind and usually a blanket, the blankets that we were given as assistance, as aid from the UNHCR.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the shape of the window frame? In other words, was it a sash-type window that you lowered and raised or was it a hinged window that opened outwards or what? In January of 1994.

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Hinge-type windows. Two sides to the window opening on hinges towards the inside of the room.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In January of 1994, did each of these sides have glass?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: One side did; the other had sheeting, some sheeting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which side had the glass, as you stood in the dining-room and looked out?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: The left-hand side, looking outwards from the room.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the nature of the covering on the right-hand side? What material? What type of material was it?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: It was foil sheeting, and we were given that by the UNHCR, too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "foil," what type of material?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Plastic foil, and it had some strings in it to reinforce it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us how thick the plastic was? Was it very thin, thin, reasonably thick, or what?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: It was thin.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it a type of plastic which usually had another purpose?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I'd never seen plastic sheeting of that type before until we were given it by the UNHCR.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it clear plastic or opaque plastic?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it possible to see through the plastic?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Just the light. You could just see some light coming through, but you couldn't see much, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned a blind. What was the blind made of?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: It was the standard type of cotton blind.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it intact or did it have any tears or holes in it, in January of 1994?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: There were holes in it, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did they come to be there?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: From the bullets, the shrapnel, all sorts of things.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the day of the 11th of January, 1994, what did you do?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: I was in my company, working. I was doing some work that day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you refer to "company," what do you mean?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: The company where I worked, where I work today and where I worked before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you mean by that your work as a building maintenance worker?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What time, approximately, did you arrive home after that work?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: About 7.00 in the evening.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was there when you arrived home?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: My wife, my children, and my neighbour, Josip Soldo, and they were sitting in the dining-room at the table.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did any members of that group seated at the table in your dining-room have their backs to the window?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: My wife and my daughter, who was sitting next to my wife. They had their backs turned towards the window.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you notice anything about the window?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: I noticed that they had not placed the blanket over the blind, and I criticised them for not doing so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did your apartment have electricity on that day?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there any light source in the dining-room when you arrived home?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was that?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: There was a candle on the table.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After you criticised them, did they respond? Did they say anything to you, anyone present?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, yes. My wife said, "Let's drink our coffee. Let's have a cup of coffee and we'll put the blanket up after that."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Having regard to the time of the year, January 1994, and the time that you arrived home, about 7.00 in the evening, I take it it was dark outside? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After your wife said those words to you, what then happened?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: She -- rather, my daughter made some coffee, put it on the table, and we started drinking our coffee.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And after that?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: After that, there was a shot, and what happened, happened. We weren't able to put up the blankets any more until I had come back from the hospital.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say there was a shot, did you actually hear the sound of a gun being fired?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: No. I ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you realise that there had been a shot?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: We felt a bang in the room. We all jumped up and looked at each other, wondering what had happened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please go on.

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: And then it was suddenly quiet. There wasn't any shooting, there wasn't any fighting, or anything like that. There was just this bang, and we all jumped up. My son escaped, jumped out. My daughter jumped up. I was wondering and looking around to see where the bang had come from. And my wife at that point just got up and said, "I'm finished." She took a step forward, went pale, and as she had taken this step, she went all pale and sunk to the floor. I called my neighbours. We had a car which was always on the ready, and we used the car to transport her to the hospital, but there was no help for her.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say there was no help for her, what happened to her?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: The bullet had hit her in her right shoulder blade and cut through the aorta and lodged -- and remained lodged in the body.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did she die?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm not quite sure, but probably on the way to the hospital, because she gave no signs of life. She had had an internal haemorrhage and there was no helping her. They couldn't save her.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On what date was she buried?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: The funeral was two days later, on the 13th of January, in the evening hours, at night, which was customary in Sarajevo, to have burials after dark.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Whereabouts was she buried?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: At the stadium, the auxiliary stadium Kosevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In a cemetery?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: There wasn't a cemetery before, but during the war it became a cemetery.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was it before the war?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: It was an auxiliary playing field belonging to the Kosevo stadium.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why were funerals conducted at night in Sarajevo at that stage?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Because there would be shooting at funerals, too. So it was safer at night.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I take you back to your dining-room at the time that you heard a shot. What exactly did you hear?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: I heard that something hit. You know, it was like a hit. I don't know how to explain it to you. I just heard this impact, this hitting impact in the premises and as if there was some glass breaking, but that was a very slight noise. I don't know how to explain it to you. It was all split second -- it all took place in a split second.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say that it was as if there was some glass breaking. Did you inspect at a later point --

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, a little bit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you inspect, at a later point, the window, in particular the left-hand side of the window that had glass?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you notice anything about the condition of the glass?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Later on, I examined it and noticed that at the bottom of the window, through the wooden frame, that the wooden frame had been split where the bullet had entered which killed my wife. And I noticed, as that was the only pane of glass that was left standing in the apartment, that that windowpane had been pierced, too. So I think that in fact two bullets had passed through on the occasion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've told us that one of the bullets lodged in the body of your wife. Did you discover anything about the path of the second bullet?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: The second bullet, as far as I was able to notice as a layman, I think it came through the glass and through the dining-room wall and lodged in the water -- in the door of the corridor outside, the hallway outside the apartment, the stairway.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President and Your Honours, at this stage I ask that the video for this incident be played. I think that is part of -- rather, that is Exhibit 3280.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: "THE INVESTIGATOR: Could you please take up the position where, to the best of your recollection, your wife was located when she was shot?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: [Complies] THE INVESTIGATOR: Could you please point to the location where, to the best of your recollection, the bullet came into the apartment? And if I may clarify my question, my instruction: The bullet which hit your wife, where that bullet came into the apartment. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: [Complies] THE INVESTIGATOR: Using this felt pen, could you please point to the spot where, to the best of your recollection, the second bullet came into the apartment after your wife was shot.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: [Complies] THE INVESTIGATOR: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: That's more or less. THE INVESTIGATOR: Now, could you please mark or point to the spot on the wall where, to the best of your recollection, the second bullet passed through the interior wall. You might have to use this.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: [Complies] THE INVESTIGATOR: If you can please hold your finger in that spot, I will now measure that distance from the floor using a standard centimetre measuring tape. I mark it as 97 centimetres. And I mark it as 5.5 centimetres from the door frame. Thank you. Could you please point to the spot where, to the best of your recollection, that second bullet hit the inside of your apartment door.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: [Complies] THE INVESTIGATOR: Thank you very much."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Mukanovic, was that -- did you recognise yourself in that video?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you comply with the requests of the investigator truthfully and to the best of your recollection?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did. But the only thing I can say is that the marking on the glass, because things have changed, I said it could only be slightly lower or perhaps a little to the left. It was an approximate marking. On the door frame, you can still see the ridge that the bullet had made, and perhaps on the wall you can feel where the bullet impacted. But otherwise, it could be a centimetre lower perhaps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the video filmed in September of last year, that is the year 2001?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Between the time that your wife died and the making of the video film, had your apartment been renovated?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the video, we could see some items of furniture in the dining-room, in particular some chairs under the window and a table in front of the chairs. How did the -- I withdraw that. Was there any difference in the furniture as we saw it in the video and the furniture at the time that your wife died?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: No. It's the same furniture. The same table; the same chairs. It's all the same.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there any difference in the position of those items of furniture in the dining-room as they appeared in the video compared to the time that your wife was shot?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: No. It's -- it was the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I ask the witness be shown the following exhibits, photographs P3237 through to P3242. Perhaps the first of those photographs could be placed on the -- placed firstly in front of the witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Mukanovic, have you made three statements with the assistance of investigators from the Prosecutor's office at the Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was one of those statements signed by you on the 27th of June of last year?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the time that you made your statement, did you also look at some photographs and black-and-white photocopies of the photographs?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The original photographs, as they appeared before you, were in colour?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you place the markings on the black-and-white copies with a red pen?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the date that you made those markings with a red pen, did you place your signature and the date on the reverse of each of the photographs, both the colour copies and the black-and-white copies?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please look at photo marked 1A which is Exhibit P3237. Does that show a view from your dining-room looking out the window?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Perhaps that could be placed -- all right. Could that be placed briefly on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please now turn to photograph marked 1B. That's Exhibit P3238.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Could that photograph be placed on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is the black-and-white version of photograph 1A; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, starting at the bottom left-hand corner of the photograph, I think you've placed a cross on the table, and alongside it, an arrow leading to the letter "A." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you read the word that you've placed under the letter "A."

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Table.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said in your evidence earlier that the candle was on the table.

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember approximately where on the table the candle was located at the time your wife was shot?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: It was about somewhere in the centre of the table.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Moving up --

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: I couldn't tell you exactly, but it was standing on the table.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Moving up the left-hand side, you've placed a circle on a part of the seat, which doesn't appear in the ELMO because it's dark, and then an arrow going directly to the left.

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the letter "D" and the name of your wife; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Moving further up the left-hand side, there is a cross on the windowpane, that is, the left side of the window as one looks out from the dining-room. Would you please read the word that appears under the letter "B" in relation to that cross.

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Glass, pane of glass.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does the cross have any particular significance in terms of its position on the glass?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: No. It just shows that this is a pane of glass.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. I'll come back to the next entry on the left-hand side shortly, but turning now to the right-hand side, you've placed a circle on the seat under the window, to the right of where your wife was seated as one looks out the window from within, and alongside that circle is the letter "E"; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And underneath the letter "E," is that the name of one of your children?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, of my daughter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. And does that indicate where she was seated at the time that your wife was shot?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the same way as "D" indicates where your wife was seated at the time that she was shot?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Towards the top of the right-hand side appears the letter "C," and it refers to a pen marking in the -- on the edge of the window. What is the word which appears under the letter "C"?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Foil sheeting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And does that indicate the half of the window that was covered in that sheeting by plastic sheeting?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. This was the side that was -- the part of the window that was covered with foil.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll return now to the letter "F." What does the area marked as letter "F" -- what is that area marked with the letter "F"?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Hrasno Brdo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And on what side of the confrontation line at the time your wife was shot was Hrasno Brdo?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: What do you mean, on which side?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it on the same side of the confrontation line as where you lived, or on the other side, or in between? I'll withdraw that question. During the armed conflict in Sarajevo, was there a boundary between the opposing armies, a front line?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You will recall that I asked you some questions earlier about where that line was in relation to your apartment.

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: It was -- the view was such that from the apartment, we were looking straight at it, the hill.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you mean by that that the hill was on the other side of the confrontation line, that is, on the side occupied by the VRS?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. The top of the hill, up to about middle of the hill, was under the control of the Serb army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In whose control was the part of the hill that you have marked with the letter "F" in the photograph?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: The upper part was under the control of the Serb army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was the lower part under the control of the Bosnian government army?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please now turn to photograph 2A, which is P3239. Does that appear to be a telephoto shot which includes that same part of the hill as viewed from within your dining-room?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Perhaps the photograph could be placed briefly on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please now turn to the black-and-white photocopy of photograph 2A, and that is marked 2B.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And perhaps that could be placed on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have marked the top of the hill, Hrasno Brdo, in photograph 2B; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you read the words which appear -- I withdraw that. Would you read the words that you wrote on that photograph, please.

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Aggressor's army positions, Hrasno Brdo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And again, by "aggressor's army," do you mean the VRS?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: It's the Serb army. The Army of Republika Srpska was the name given to it later. But the terms get mixed up, so I don't know what to call what, when.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Would you now look at photograph 3A. By comparing it to photograph 2A, is it apparent that it is a further telephoto shot of the same hill, or at least part of that hill, as viewed from your dining-room window?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In a similar fashion, did you mark the photocopy of that photograph, which is photograph 3B, so as to indicate the part of the hill that was occupied by the Serb army at the time your wife was shot?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: If 3B could be placed on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll repeat that question. In relation to the portion of the hill which appears in that photograph, did you mark with the red pen that part which was occupied by the Serb army at the time your wife was shot?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, at this stage I'd ask that the 360-degree photograph be displayed, that is, Exhibit number 3279.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed. May I remind you, Mr. Ierace, that in your revised schedule it's three quarters of an hour scheduled for the witness, as far as I see, and ...

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I'll attempt to move a little faster.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, looking at the image in front of you on the computer screen --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I think there's an objection, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I apologise, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. Thank you for giving us the floor. We still have the same problem. I believe that I heard yesterday that my learned colleague Mr. Mundis said that he would get us a witness to tell us how these photographs were produced, and I believe that it would be good that we get some kind of technical briefing that would tell us about the quality of these photographs rather than go on, witness by witness, using these photographs. I think that we should have started the other way around. And the Defence is objecting to the photographs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think we had a general explanation how these photographs were produced, although not in testimony by a witness who produced them. But we were explained, as far as I remember, rather in detail, on how this was produced. Is there any -- is it a matter of formality that you want to have this formally confirmed by a witness, or is there any technical thing you do not understand about these photographs?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I believe that I have no competence whatever in technical matters, and I certainly need all the assistance I can get. However, in this particular case, the Defence doesn't know to which extent it can trust these photographs since it has not had a technical briefing, a presentation about these photographs. And I believe that Mr. Mundis proposed to have a witness who would tell us all about this. So it would be good to have that before using these photographs so that we know whether we can reject them or not and before we actually have the witnesses looking at the photographs as shown by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, I remember that prior to the examination of the first witness on a -- one of the scheduled incidents - I remember it was someone who was gardening his plot - it was rather in detail explained to us how this was all created. I do not understand what additional information you expect from a witness who would say, "Well, I did stand on the yellow cross. I ..." Are you interested to know what exactly the lenses were or -- I mean, I try to understand your problem and see what would be added at this moment if we -- if we would get the confirmation of someone who will confirm that it was he who made the computer programme.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. We know that nowadays we can use technical equipment to produce virtual pictures. And when we have witnesses who are looking at the photographs, they're not quite sure. So what we would quite like to see is to have a sort of summary and a briefing about how these photographs were produced so that we could have this checked by our own experts, and if there are any technical problems, and at that time we can then look at it in this way. But here, if we take these for granted, these photographs, I don't think that is really on. But it is -- it is technical question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... in this courtroom, as you'll understand. May I ask the Prosecution, since this seems to be a problem for the Defence: Would it be possible - I'm just asking about possibilities - that you would call the witness you had in mind to call later and give all the technical explanations in addition to what you explained to us already, Mr. Ierace?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Excuse me one moment, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. That could be done. Might I point out that we have taken steps to include the Prosecution [sic] as much as possible in the shooting of the videos and the photographs. Ms. Pilipovic attended the filming of some of the videos in Sarajevo in September of last year. I provided an explanation as to how the videos and photographs were made to her then. I have done so briefly in the opening, and I did so again last Friday week. I think Mr. Piletta-Zanin was not present on that occasion. Mr. President, this is -- or, rather, yesterday, I think, was the first time there has been an objection articulated by the Defence so as to refer to the reliability of the images. I'm happy to accommodate them. I would point out that of course each witness who has come along, who has appeared in the videos and identified themselves and also given evidence in relation to the images which appear in the 360-degree photographs. I have this difficulty: that the witness involved will ultimately give testimony on a number of matters to do with video footage, including the footage which appeared in the opening, as to when that footage was obtained as well as the editing process. It may be that in order to accommodate my friends, his evidence could be given in two stages. That is, we could call him perhaps later this week to give an explanation from the witness box as to the process involved, and then at a later point he could be recalled to give more detailed information, more technical information which we wish to bring from him and evidence as to the means by which we came by the footage used in the opening. So that course would at least equip my friends at this stage, shortly after they first raised the issue, with an explanation in the Trial Chamber as to, in particular, the method by which the photographs were joined together electronically so as to make the 360-degree image. I'll make some inquiries later on today and perhaps -- there's a meeting already arranged between ourselves and the Defence at 2.30 this afternoon. I'll discuss it with them on that occasion and inform the Trial Chamber perhaps tomorrow as to whether we could amend our schedule of witnesses so as to include that witness later this week. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Thank you, Mr. President. To begin with, I'm not quite sure that I fully understand what my learned friend was saying, but I think he only made a slight slip of the tongue. I'm looking at what Mr. Ierace has said. He said that he was including the "Prosecution" in the shooting as much as possible. It was merely for the sake of precision. It is line 13. And perhaps it would be good if this witness came towards the end of the week so that we could hear it. And we have not had the opportunity to see him. I think that the Defence will be ready for the -- was for the meeting last week, but it was not possible. But here we are. At any rate, we are at the disposal of the Prosecution whenever they want to have a meeting and to describe this video, this editing, and to take stock of the whole procedure that was done. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber allows the Prosecution to continue showing the 360-degrees photograph. We'll think about a possible change in the order of calling the witnesses and whether we would suggest you to do so, since I do understand that you would be able to split up the testimony of the witness in two and start with the technical aspects and then only later on have a confirmation of times of obtaining the materials, the video materials, the photo materials, which of course would cover many other incidents as well. The reason why we allow you to continue at this moment is that, apart from a general objection that there has been no opportunity to verify the technique used in producing the material, we did not hear any specific objection as to why there would be something wrong in the production of the materials. But the sooner everyone in this courtroom is Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. informed about the technical details, the better it might be. May I just ask you: Is this witness available in this country, or should we fly him in from abroad, or have you got no idea?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, this witness is probably one of the most convenient witnesses for us to call because he works in the building.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Of course, in calling him at short notice, I won't be able to provide a statement as to what he will say beforehand because that process is continuing --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Of course. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: -- but I'll do that. Might I, simply while I'm on my feet, also point out that my friend is correct in relation to the reference to "Prosecution."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That was a clear mistake.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So we'll allow you to continue with this 360-degrees photograph, and pay attention to the technical aspects as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Mukanovic, looking at the image on your screen at the moment, is that the view in one direction from your dining-room window?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do we see the hill of Hrasno Brdo between two apartment blocks slightly to the left of the centre of the image?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: We do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Slightly to the right of centre, do we see a mosque?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: We do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Apart from the area that you marked on the photographs of the part of Hrasno Brdo which was in the control of the Serb army, was any other part of the image in front of you controlled by the Serb army at the time your wife was shot?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: No. I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Could the image please be panned to the right. Please pause there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do we see now on the left-hand side of the image the frame of the dining-room window; slightly to the right of centre, the doorway leading into the kitchen of your apartment?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Please continue to pan the image to the right. Pause there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do we now see, towards the centre of the image, the doorway leading out of your dining-room towards the entrance to the apartment, and in the foreground the table, or a table?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Please continue to pan the image to the right. Pause there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Again, apart from the top of Hrasno Brdo, was any other part of the image in front of you controlled by the Serb army at the time that your wife was shot?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: No. Except for that hill up there, nothing else can be seen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: By "that hill," do you mean the hill which appears on the right-hand side of the image, on the horizon?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Perhaps the image could be panned slightly to the right. Stop there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is that the same hill, that is, the same part of the hill that you marked on the photographs that you saw earlier?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. I ask that the witness be shown Exhibit P3235, which is a map. Might the part of the map which is marked in pink be placed on the ELMO, after the witness has seen it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was your first statement dated the 23rd of November, 1995?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the time you made that statement, did you place some markings on a map, which appears in front of you?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you mark with a cross inside a circle the position of your apartment at the time your wife was shot?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. If the map could be placed back on the -- no, no. I think the witness has already done that. Please don't mark the map.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you see the cross with the circle on it on the map?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And I ask that the part of the map which has the -- I withdraw that. That's right. Thank you. If the map could be stopped at that position.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll ask that question again. Yes. Do you now point to the cross inside a circle which denotes --

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: This is the building, the building that I live in.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you use a pink pen to mark the position of the part of the confrontation lines at the time that your wife was shot?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please point to the pink line that you marked.

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: It's this line here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, did you place some blue marks on the other side of the pink line to indicate the ridge of Hrasno Brdo that you identified in the photographs?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please indicate those blue marks.

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: It's these ones here, and this one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. I think you first placed the pointer on some blue marks that appear right alongside the pink line; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Place the pointer back there again.

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Just pause there for a moment. Now, do you see that you have placed the blue marks on a street which, according to the map, is Ozrenska Street? Is that the case?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. It is down there, because you can't see Ozrenska Street from my apartment because it is higher up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, in relation to the other two blue points, did you place alongside them the numbers 1 and 2?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. In the interests of saving time: Do they refer to sources of fire, to your knowledge, during the armed conflict?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What building or buildings do those numbers denote? What do they refer to?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: This building number 1, that I marked number 1, this is the skyscrapers of the shopping centre, as you call it, on Grbavica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And 2?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: And this here is the building of the water management administration.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To your knowledge, during the armed conflict were there any particular places in Sarajevo that received fire from either of those two sources?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: The snipers used to fire from the shopping centre at this intersection here, at Dolac Malta.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "intersection," I think you pointed at a crossing over the Miljacka River. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, the bridge here, this bridge over the Miljacka, and the intersection next to it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, you've told us that you were in the army, and you've also told us that you were living at home, sleeping at home. Is that the case? Residing at home?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, where did you feel safer: at the front line or away from the front line, elsewhere in Sarajevo, during the armed conflict?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: I was safer, I felt more secure, on the front line.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why was that?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. I suppose the confrontation lines were near, and therefore fire was opened less often.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do you mean by saying "fire was opened less often" at the confrontation lines? Less often than where?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Than around the city.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Just two final matters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that your son was aged 15 and your daughter 17 when your wife was killed. Was your son going to school?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Whereabouts?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: In the building itself. They couldn't go to the school on Hrasno, so that classes were organised - elementary school classes, that is, because he was still in the elementary school - and these classes were organised in buildings, in cellars. So there was a room in our small building, and they did it there. And the children from adjoining buildings came there to our building, and that is where they had their classes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the day and evening that your wife was killed, what were you wearing? What type of clothing?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Civilian clothes. So I had a sweater, I think, and blue trousers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was your wife wearing when she was shot? I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: My wife was in a house frock, a pajama.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How old was your wife?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Thirty-eight, I think. Thirty-seven, thirty-eight.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was your wife's full name?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Hatema.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recollect what the weather was like at the time that you arrived home?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: It was quiet, calm. You mean the weather, whether there was any precipitation or ...?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: No. It was quiet. There was no rain, nothing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any military units inside your building at that stage when your wife was killed?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there people other than -- I withdraw that. Were there any military targets of which you were aware, such as military equipment or troops, nearby your apartment on the date that your wife was killed?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had there been any shooting or shelling earlier that evening in the area of your apartment, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: No. That day, as far as I know, it was pretty quiet, one of the calmer days, because there were other days when there would be fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Looking at the clock, Ms. Pilipovic, I think it's better to have a break now, and if you are then ready for cross-examination when we resume.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mukanovic, we'll have a break now, and after the break you're examined by counsel for the Defence. We'll have a break until 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, during the break I spoke with some members of my team who informed me that they have been told by the Victims and Witnesses Unit that there is likely to be a problem with travel arrangements for a witness or witnesses that were expected to arrive tonight. The unit is preparing a written memorandum explaining the nature of those difficulties. In essence, they relate to arrangements between, as I understand it, the Dutch Foreign Ministry and the authorities in Bosnia. I draw Your Honours' attention to that at this stage because it may be relevant to Your Honours' deliberations on whether you wish the Prosecution to call the relevant witness to explain the production and editing of the videos and 360-degree photographs. Might I respectfully suggest that that is most likely to impact on our programme for this Thursday. Thank you. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, if you would. We discussed the matter briefly, and I think the Chamber is of the opinion that if the Defence has any problems in understanding the technicalities of the -- especially the 360-degree photographs, then it should be clarified as soon as possible. So if you would please prepare for calling the witness who will specifically testify on these technical aspects, and that might fill in the gap which would prevent us to waste any time. Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Thank you, Mr. President. May I just add the following: I said at the very beginning that there were problems of informatics and computers, and there was a letter from Mr. Ierace, and this type of photograph, for example, if it was given to us in disk form, we always have technical problems in reading it in, in accessing it. So if we have problems, and of course everybody can have problems, let me just say that the system is not as safe as a simple photographic system, so we have to bear that in mind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I could not confirm that if you have a problem, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, that of course everyone may have a problem, that's right. Whether they'll have a problem is a different thing. But let me just ask the Prosecution. If you have, as far as I can see, a system which enables you to manipulate at least the picture, so that means you have two elements, first of all the programme enabling you to manipulate and then of course the data on the picture itself. Would it be possible to provide the -- to provide the Defence also with both the programme and the photos so that they can at least at home see what happens on the screen? It might not solve all the problems but --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, as I understand it, the only software that is required to play the 360-degree photograph is Quicktime, which is freely available to be downloaded on the Internet, and legally, as I understand it. But if my friends are experiencing a problem in opening that photograph, then I anticipate that's where the problem exists, in not having the appropriate software. I would be prepared to make the relevant witness available to the Defence to explain the process before he gives his evidence in lieu of a statement so they have some idea as to what it is he will say, and it may be that problems such as this can be overcome in those discussions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I hope it will. And of course, nevertheless, the testimony of the witness explaining the technical aspects, we can expect that soon. I'll give it a try on my computer as well so to see as where we come, if you -- Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. Well, that is very good to choose a witness who could also explain to us why the entirety of the system wasn't working, which was something that was recognised, of course, indirectly by the Prosecution. But I'm sure that all of us will be able to move forward. It was not an error on the part of the Defence but a system which is largely deficient. Thank you in advance anyway.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I leave the qualification as far as the systems to you, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, but we will now continue with the examination of the witness. Mr. Mukanovic, I have to apologise for dealing with all kind of technical issues which interrupts your examination. Your examination, of course I do understand that the events you're testifying about are of far greater importance than any of the technical problems we are facing here in this courtroom. So this Chamber, and I think the parties also, will now again fully concentrate on what you have to tell us because that's the main reason why you're present here. And just forget that we have to solve now and then some technical problems which are of a minor nature compared to the story you are telling us. Please proceed. Ms. Pilipovic. You understood what I mean, Mr. Mukanovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I do. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, thank you. Cross-examined by Ms. Pilipovic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, may I start off by saying good day to you. And could you approach the microphone for us to be able to hear you better? Thank you. During the examination-in-chief today asked by my learned colleague, you said that you had given to the investigators of the Prosecution three statements; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell me whether you gave a statement on the 4th of September, 2000?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: No. 2000? Yes, 2000. In the year 2000.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you make a statement on the 23rd of November, 1995, as well?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And together with that statement -- or, rather, in that statement you explain something that you confirmed. And it is Defence [as interpreted] Exhibit P3236. You were also asked about photographs, some photographs today. On the 10th of June, 2001, did you make a statement to the investigators of the Prosecution, giving them an explanation and a clarification of the photographs you were shown today?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. You said that you were employed before the conflict broke out, and that was a question asked by my learned colleague. Could you tell us what firm, what company you worked for?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: UNIS.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us in what part of town the company was located?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Marin Dvor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Asked by my learned colleague whether you had changed your employment or work in the course of the war, your answer was no; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but I don't know in what sense you mean.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you work in the work organisation located in the UNIS building throughout?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us, please, whether in 1992 you worked in the UNIS building.

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us, please, what your profession is.

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: I am a maintenance worker for the central heating system.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me remind you that you said that during the conflict you did not change your employment, your work; you were a maintenance worker for the heating system; you continued to be a maintenance worker for the heating system. Is that what you said?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were asked whether, in the course of the conflict, you changed the work you did, you changed your employment, could you tell us when the conflict actually came about in Sarajevo, according to you?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: In April 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us today that you lived in a part of town which is called Hrasno; is that right?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In April, May 1992, did you go to work to your company, in the company you worked for?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Not in May.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In April?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us, please, why you didn't go to your workplace in May.

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Quite simply, we weren't able to reach Marin Dvor to get there, because of the barracks. There would be shooting from those barracks, and we weren't able to pass by that way. And the trams weren't working, neither was any other form of transport at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In May of that year, 1992, in the part of town called Hrasno where you lived, was there anything unusual going on, anything unusual that happened there? Was there a conflict in your part of town in May?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us, please, whether, and when, the conflict broke out in your part of town.

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: In the part of town that I lived in, there wasn't any conflict. The conflict occurred at Grbavica, further off, and Hrasno Brdo, and some demarcation lines, where there was some kind of demarcation going on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us, please, what this demarcation was, and between whom, if you know, if you're able to tell us, of course.

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. Probably between the army and the civilians, as far as I'm able to gather, self-organised civilians who were trying to prevent the army from entering the city.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "self-organised civilians," do you mean that this took part in your part of town, that there were self-organised civilians in your part of town as well?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you happen to know whether there were any of these self-organised civilians in the part of town that is called Grbavica?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I was never up there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us, please, whether, in 1992, in the part of town where you yourself lived, that is to say Hrasno, whether the civilians had organised themselves, whether this self-organisation of civilians ever came about.

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. To tell you the truth, I never paid attention to things like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you say you don't know that in 1992, in the part of town called Hrasno, the civilians undertook the process of self-organisation?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. Probably. There was the reserve police force, and a civilian protection system was organised of some kind.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the examination-in-chief and a question from my learned friend, you said that you were a member of the army, that you became a member of the BH army in April 1993.

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us, please, what military formation you belonged to when you joined the BH army.

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: The 1st Mountain Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us, please, where the command post of the 1st Mountain Brigade was located, the one to which you belonged.

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: At Bistrik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How much time would you spend -- how much time did you spend in the army from April to the 1st of January? How long would you spend up at the front lines? During the time that you were in the army, how much time did you spend up at the front lines, day, week, month? How much time would you spend up at the front line?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Usually 24 hours. Then we would go home for a rest.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us, please, what kind of uniforms -- or rather, did the BH army have uniforms?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Very rarely. Very few.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us, please, whether the BH army had any insignia of any kind or anything that you wore which would denote your membership in the army.

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: We were just issued some sort of coats of arms or insignia, but usually we would be in civilian clothing. We didn't have any uniforms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also said that you were a member of the 101st Mountain Brigade and that the command post was at Bistrik. Did I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: The 1st Mountain, and afterwards it changed. Whether it was the 1st or whether it was the 2nd later on, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I apologise. So you said the 1st Mountain Brigade; is that right?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you tell us where the positions of your 1st Mountain Brigade were? Where did you go to take up your position when you were at the front lines?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: At Trebevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you were at the positions at Trebevic, could you tell us more specifically where those positions were located on Mount Trebevic.

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: I personally was to the left of the path. It was a place called Kosmatica. That was the name of the slope, the area, Kosmatica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, please, whether at those front lines where you Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. yourself were deployed, were there any trenches?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us, please, who dug those trenches?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: We did. We dug the trenches ourselves mostly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you, in April 1993, joined up, when you join the BH army, were you issued any weapons?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I understand you correctly, while you were up at the front line, you had no weapons?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did, at the front line.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From April 1993, when you joined the BH army, how long did you dig trenches up at the front line where you yourself were deployed?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: We would always do a bit of digging, fixing some things. We would also always do a bit of digging, fix up the trenches.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From the place where the command post was, and you said it was at Bistrik, and you said you would spend 24 hours at the front line, does that mean that you were off for 24 hours after that?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us where you spent those 24 hours off?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: At home or in the company, if necessary. Sometimes I would go to work in the company if the need arose.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us, from the command post to your apartment, how did you go back home?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: On foot; I walked.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how did you get to the command post?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Also on foot.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us: In that 101st Brigade, were there any battalions?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you belong to any of those battalions?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us how many battalions there were?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us how many men the battalions numbered, a battalion numbered?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the command post, the command post of your particular battalion? Was that at Bistrik, too?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't think so. I think it was up close to the front line.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence would like to have the witness shown a map, it is Prosecution Exhibit 3235, because the Defence would like to ask the witness a few questions regarding the map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, do you have the map in front of you which you used during your answers in the examination-in-chief and the colleagues -- and the questions asked by my learned colleagues?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You explained to us today that the mauve colour or violet colour denotes the front line.

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us when the front line was established as you have marked it?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you be more specific? When in 1992? What month?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: In the summer, probably. Sometime in the summer of 1992. Perhaps before. I really don't know, but I know that the line was set up there, and it was there all the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us the name of the street on the map by this purple colour or mauve colour where you have Hrasno to the left and the blue spot marked on the map? Do you know what the name of the street is?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: I can't remember now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I tell you that it says Djuraskovica Street, is that the street? Milutin Djuraskovica.

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it might be what was before. But what it's called now, I really can't say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you have just said that in Milutin Djuraskovica Street, that that was where the front line was; is that right?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that ever since it was established in 1992 up until 1994 and 1995, it was not changed; is that right?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us the distance between the lines, the front lines; that is to say, the -- being held by the BH army and the line controlled by the army of Republika Srpska? In that particular street, what was the distance?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, just the street. The street divided them. On one side of the street was the BH army in the houses there, and the other side of the street was the Serb army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "in the buildings," the buildings that the BH army was in, now, on your side as it was the part of town you lived in, could you tell us what buildings there were in that street held by the BH army?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: I can't tell you the names of the buildings. I know that the long building was probably the one that the BH army was in, and then those first buildings right up by the road.
