And also on the other side, in the buildings across the road, was the Serb army. The petrol pump and the other buildings on the other side of the street, that's where the Serb army was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us whether the buildings in the Hrasno area under the control of the BH army, were these apartment buildings where the BH army was?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: I really don't know, but I believe that they had been evacuated, all of them. Those were the -- right by the front line.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So in those -- the buildings were mostly occupied by the BH army?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I'm not sure, but I believe that the civilians had been evacuated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us to which formation the BH army soldiers belong in that part of Hrasno under the control of the BH army?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: There in Hrasno, I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On this part of the front line, and you said it was just a street, were there trenches?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you go to that front line?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether on that -- in that part of town, in Hrasno and Grbavica, there was fighting between the two sides, between two armies?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, on several occasions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us and you indicated on that map that you live in the 27th of July Street.

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is the distance between your street and the Hero Square, Trg Heroja, in Hrasno?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. Maybe 300, 400 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that on the Hero Square, more specifically in the Loris building, was the headquarters of the BH army?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. Maybe that was the first building straight by the front line.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you marked the map, when you marked the front line on the map, we were just talking about the Milutin Djuraskovica Street, and you extended that line, and the line goes up to the Grbavica stadium, if I am reading this correctly.

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, by the stadium.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It goes towards Ozrenska Street and then it goes on further to the left.

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us, in relation to this part of the front line, what was the distance between the warring sides?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Honestly, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During 1992, did you go to this front line?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge that in this area of the city where the lines were, that there was fighting in that area?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. As far as I know, on several occasions: once by the stadium, once up on the hill.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us whether these lines, as they are established, that they -- would you agree with me if I say that they divided this part of town?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that in the part of town that we are talking about, the Hrasno area, from your side of the line, that that area was under the control of the BH army and that this area was mostly inhabited by ethnic Muslims?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: There were other ethnicities as well, not only Muslims. They were in a minority, but there were others.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know about the ethnic composition of the area in the city, the part of the city Grbavica, in Milutin Djuraskovica Street, which was under the control of the Republika Srpska army, where the majority were Serbs?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know what you mean. Do you mean before the war, in the war itself?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Specifically before the front lines were established.

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: No. I couldn't tell you, because we never followed who lived where, who was majority, who was minority.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After the front lines were established, did they establish also an ethnic division of the city?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, roughly speaking.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you told us today about the -- with regard to the photographs, and this is the Prosecution Exhibit P3237, on these photographs, you were explaining where things were in your apartment. Could you tell us about the position that your wife was sitting in, your daughter, and yourself when you came into the apartment.

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: They were sitting when I arrived.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they drinking coffee at the time when you arrived?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After you arrived, how long afterwards did your late wife make coffee?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, approximately after I arrived. They waited for me to come home, and they knew I was supposed to come, so they were waiting for me. So shortly after I arrived.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us, if you can recall, what the time was.

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: When I came home, it was about 1900 hours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The moment when you heard the bang in your apartment, were you in the process -- is that while you were drinking coffee or had you already finished drinking coffee?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: We were drinking coffee.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will now go back to the map, and you marked -- you made a marking on the map, in blue, the locations of the buildings that you identified as the buildings where the shooting had come from, and "1" you marked the building of the water management administration.

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Could you remind me? Under "1" --

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: These are skyscrapers in the shopping centre in Grbavica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Under "2," you marked that this was a building --

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Of the water management administration.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you tell us how tall, how high is the water management administration building, how many floors it has?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: About ten, maybe.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To a question asked by my learned colleague, you said that it was from these buildings that the shooting was done.

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what weapons were used to shoot?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Sniper rifles.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us, in relation to your place of residence, to where you lived, the buildings that were on the front line that was under the control of the BH army, which is the Hrasno area of the city, were there also snipers shooting from those positions towards the position where the shopping centre was?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you were in the BH army, from April 1993 until the 1st of Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. January, 1996, in the formations of the BH army, were there snipers?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: I really don't know. I was on the front line. I was standing guard. And there, where we were, we had no snipers. We were in a wood, where a sniper wouldn't help you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you have no knowledge whether in that area of the city, Hrasno, under the control of the BH army, whether there were snipers?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you indicate for us on the map the place called Bistrik and the street, if you know, if you know which street it was where the command post of your brigade was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we perhaps first zoom out so that we can ... Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, could you use a black marker to mark the location on the map, the location of Bistrik, please.

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, for the record, the witness made a circular marking on the map as being the command post of the brigade, by making a circle going under the Obala Pariske Komune Street.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, did I understand this correctly, the location that you've marked of the command post?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: It's just Bistrik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Above the word "Bistrik" and between the words "Obala Pariske Komune"?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know what the street was called. It's probably here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you just make a slightly thicker marking, and if you could mark a number "1", please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please have another marker, because this one doesn't function well. Is there not any other black marker? There must be a black marker somewhere in this courthouse. Could anyone -- Judge El Mahdi at least has a black marker. It's not a thick one, but if could you give this to -- my fountain pen never functions, so it would not be of great help. Yes, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, looking at the last half dozen questions and answers, it's certainly unclear to me what it is that the witness has marked. He was invited to mark "The location on the map, the location of Bistrik, please." That's page 49, line 8. He purported to do that and then he was asked this question:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, did I understand this correctly, the location that you've marked of the command post.

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: It's just Bistrik. So the questions really direct themselves to two separate issues. Perhaps --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, if we look a few lines before, the question was:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you indicate for us on the map the place called Bistrik, which has been mentioned by the -- and the street, if you know, if you know which street it was where the command post of your brigade was. And I do agree with you that later on it was just -- Ms. Pilipovic was just referring to Bistrik, but of course she explained before. But let's just clarify it. The place that you just indicated by putting a circle, Mr. Mukanovic, was that the place where the command post was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, this would clarify what the witness did. Please proceed, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, could you, in relation to the location you've marked as being the command post of the brigade, could you mark for us where the front line was where you went to your own, so to speak, command post? Could you mark that for us? In which direction did you go to your command post?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you also -- could you just make a marking with a black felt-tip pen, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We've solved the problem. We have a thick marker now, Mr. Mukanovic. Will you please use the thick marker.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I appreciate you want a minimum of objections, but the witness has just been asked to do two quite separate things in the one question: First of all, to mark where the front line was "when you went to your own," and then it's immediately followed by a second question, "In which direction did you go to your command post?" I assume that the last question is an invitation to indicate how he travelled from his residence to his command post. If that's the case, it assumes there was the one route taken every time. In any event, I'd ask that my friend split the two questions into -- so that the witness isn't invited to do two things in the one question. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you please guide the witness to do one thing at the same time.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, when you -- when you went to your front line, to your position, to your post, did you first go to the command post?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Not always. Mostly, I didn't. I would go straight to the front line.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us where the front line was where you were.

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us, from your house to the front line that you've marked as being your front line where you were, what was the route that you -- that you would take? What was the front line that passed that you indicated -- the front line that you said you spent 24 hours at?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: We went around, around the city, all around and then up Bistrik, and then we would try and get to it through different routes on the hill.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you mark for us on the map when you would come to your -- to the post at the command? How would you get from the command post to the front line? What confrontation line would you cross to get to the place which was -- which was your military post? Could you explain for -- show us with the map your post? Which route did you take to get to your post?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, it's not quite clear to me at this moment. You asked whether the witness would first go to the command post when he'd go to the front line, and then he said: "Not always. Mostly I didn't. I would go straight to the front line." Are you now asking the witness to indicate when he went to his post before going to the front line or after returning to the front line, what route he was taking or -- it's not quite clear to me what.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, my question whether he -- whether he went to his post, to his military post from his apartment, whether he would go to the command post. The answer given by the witness was that he didn't. Mostly, that he -- sometimes he would go to the command and then go to the line and that sometimes he would go directly from his apartment to the line. And he told us which route he took to get from his apartment to the line. So now I would like to know from the witness, from the command post, when he arrived at the command post, which route would he take to get to the front line where he was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I understand. From the command post to his position at the front line.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, could you show -- could you indicate for us on this map what was the route that you took from the command post that you've marked up to the front line where you had your post?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: We mostly went up Bistrik and then we would take different side streets.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you just mark it for us with a marker on the map, the part of the route that you took?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, I do not understand. He did not always take the same route, so it's very difficult to mark, Ms. Pilipovic. I don't know whether you want him to mark all the routes he ever took or -- would you please be more precise?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you go to the front line from the command post that you have made on the map, the location that you indicated on the map? Did you always take the same route?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you would take different routes.

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you took all these different routes, were there trenches in those different streets that you would take?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would now like to return to the photographs that we used to make certain explanations by the witness. I would like the witness to be shown photograph 2A.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you have before you photograph 2A. Can you tell us, in relation to the building that we see in the middle, and above it we see structures which on the photograph 2B you said were the positions of the army of Republika Srpska. Can you tell us if these buildings and these houses existed in this same shape, in this same condition in 1992 and 1993?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: These buildings were there. Up on the hill there are buildings which were built recently.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge if in this part where there are newly built houses and where we also see some old houses, do you know who lived there in 1992, 1993, and 1994? Or let me be more precise. Do you know who those houses belonged to? When I say "who they belonged to," I'm asking whether their owners were Serbs or Muslims.

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know, really. I think it was all mixed up there.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence would like to show the witness the photograph 2B. That is a black-and-white photograph which the witness marked as 2B. So photograph 2B.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, on this photograph, in relation to this line underneath which you -- where you made some bars, was that the front line? Do you have any knowledge of that?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us how far -- what was the distance between the front lines of the two sides in this part? We did not -- is it that you don't know or --

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: No, I don't know. I don't know exactly what the distance was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have just told us that you have never been up there, so why did you mark the line here? How did you know that? How do you know that this was the front line controlled by the army of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Because from these positions which I marked here, fire came as often as not, fire aimed at the bridge, at the intersection. It was usually of evening. One could see because they would be using tracing bullets. So you could see where the fire came from.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, in relation to these houses that you can see here, if this is the Ozrensak street, in this part here?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: No. Ozrenska Street is up there on the top.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, since you've told us that from your apartment to the place that you said the fire came from, as the crow flies, was 800 metres --

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Well, I'd say so. I'm not sure that I got it right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. But can you tell us how long is the earth road from the place where your apartment is to the place where you say were the positions of the army of Bosnian Serbs? How many kilometres or metres?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. Believe me, I never went up those roads. I don't know where they lead. I just don't know, I really don't. I made this assessment looking through my window, and that is why I gave you the figure, but that was it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That day when the incident happened and when your wife died, the 11th of January, 1994, did you report the incident to the authorised body?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us who that was? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: We reported it to the police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us where is the place, in relation to your apartment, where the police is, the building that you went to, to report?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: The police was across the river, across the Miljacka. I apologise. At that time, the police was across the Miljacka, near the river -- near the church. Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mean that in Hrasno, in that part of the town that you lived in, there were no police stations?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: No, not at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us: When you went to the police station and reported the incident, did you do it that same day when it happened or could it be some other day?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: I think it was the next morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us --

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: No. I apologise. It wasn't me who reported it. It was a neighbour of mine who went there to report it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did the police come to the scene of the incident?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, you wanted to say something.

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: They came the next day, when I went to arrange things in the hospital and with a funeral and all that. They came there to conduct their investigation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you present?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, may I just consult my colleague, please, just a moment?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you told us that in 1992 there was a reserve police force in Hrasno.

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us if they were quartered in a building in Hrasno, and where?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: In early 1992, they were in the Ministry of the Interior building, that is, the police station building, next to the mosque; and then I think sometime by mid that year, they moved to another location.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge -- you mentioned this other location. You said they moved to this other location. Do you know where that was?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, thank you very much. The Defence has no more questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, is there any need to re-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. Any questions from the Bench? Judge El Mahdi has one or more questions for you, Mr. Mukanovic. JUDGE EL MAHDI: Thank you, Mr. President. Questioned by the Court: JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] Witness, I'd like us to look together at the possible trajectory of the bullet which was fired and hit your wife on the day of the incident. I'd therefore like, registrar, if you could show the witness the photograph 2B. No, I'm sorry. 1A [In English] and 1B. Can we put 1B directly, please. [Interpretation] Now, Witness, if I understand you right, the bullet went through the window frame and hit your wife, who was sitting on this settee. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: It is. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] Well, then, if one draws a straight line from the circle that you made here in red to indicate Hrasno Brdo, and I believe the trajectory would necessarily have to go down, downward, because this is higher ground. Now, my question is: Did the bullet go through the settee or not? Could you see any bullet traces on this settee, in the seat of the settee?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: No. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] But she was hit in the shoulder? Did I understand it well? Your wife, she was hit in the shoulder?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] Which was above the back of this settee, is it? Her shoulder protruded above the back of the settee?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I suppose so. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] And the second bullet that was fired, it hit the glass?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it did. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] It went through the windowpane?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I also have a question for you, Mr. Mukanovic. You told us that from April 1993 until January 1996, you joined the Bosnian army. Was this a voluntary decision of yours or were you more or less forced to join the army? Could you tell us how this happened.

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: I was called up. I was called up, I received the papers, and I reported.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you were not voluntarily going into the army, but you were just called, you were fulfilling your duty?

utterances.speaker: AKIF MUKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Mukanovic, for your answer. We have come to the end of your examination as a witness in this Court, and I think we all are aware of how painful it must have been for you to tell about a very sad moment in your life. We highly appreciate that you have come to The Hague, the far way to The Hague, to answer the questions of all the parties and of the Judges, since, for taking the decisions we'll have to take, we depend on the assistance of those who have been present at the time and at the place where the accused is charged to have acted. We thank you, therefore, very much, and we wish you a good journey home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, could you please lead the witness out of the courtroom. Madam Registrar, then we have documents to be decided upon as to their admission into evidence. I think we have -- the video is the first.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The video is P3280H.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think we then have the 360-degree photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I think we have first a series of photos. I see them in your hands.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And then, I think, finally we have the map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The map that has been marked by the witness during the examination. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, I think this would also be a good occasion to tell you that you'll be provided by the registry with a new list of Prosecution exhibits which will be limited only to those exhibits that have been admitted into evidence and that will contain a description as neutral as possible of the type of document concerned.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. I was already very kindly informed about this this morning, but once again, thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then the next witness for the Prosecution. Mr. Mundis, you are standing.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. The Prosecution calls Nafa Taric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Usher, could you please -- oh, Mr. Usher has disappeared, but ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: For the benefit of the Trial Chamber and the Defence, this witness will be testifying with respect to scheduled sniping incident number 10.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could perhaps anyone just see where the usher is so that we don't lose any ... Would there be anyone just to have a look?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please bring in the next witness, Mr. Usher. I do understand we have to wait for two or three seconds. Okay. We'll be patient.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Might I suggest, just perhaps out of a sense of expediency, that we took the break now and resumed at 12.40, 12.45.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If it's more than one or two seconds, I would then suggest that we resume at a quarter to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Taric, can you hear me in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Taric, the usher will hand out a -- the text of a declaration to you which the Rules of Procedure and Evidence require you to make prior to being examined as a witness. Will you please make that declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Please be seated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Welcome in this courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You'll first be examined by Mr. Mundis of the team of the Prosecutor who called you as a witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Examined by Mr. Mundis:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. Taric, for the record, can you please state your full name and spell your last name?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: Nafa Taric. N-a-f-a and T-a-r-i-c.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For the record, can you please state your date of birth and the town or the municipality in which you were born?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: The 2nd of June, 1958, in Prijepolje, the Prijepolje municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. Taric, to the best of your recollection, when did the war start in Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: In April.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of which year?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When the war broke out in Bosnia, can you please tell the Trial Chamber what city you were living in?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: I was living in the city of Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the name of the neighbourhood or area of Sarajevo that you lived in?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: The neighbourhood was called Hrasno.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In what year did you move to Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And have you continued to live in the city of Sarajevo since 1978?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you briefly describe for the Trial Chamber how life in the city of Sarajevo changed once the war began?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: Life in town changed completely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you be more specific or elaborate upon that answer, please?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: Freedom of movement, fear. We had to do without essentials, water, electricity, fuel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the course of --

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: Food.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the course of the war in Sarajevo, did you become aware of incidents involving sniping and/or shelling?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did become aware of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you briefly describe for the Trial Chamber how that sniping Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. and shelling affected your life?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: As for every other human being, I was afraid, like everybody else. I had to be wary in my movements, extra careful, and I moved around as little as possible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you aware of confrontation lines or front lines in the city of Sarajevo during the war?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: They changed quite a lot. So I don't really know very much about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you aware of the existence of such lines?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which military forces were poised along these front lines?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: There were the defence lines and the army, the side that attacked us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which military force was on the defence lines?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: The army of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know the name of the forces that attacked you, as you put it?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: They changed names often, but they were popularly called -- they themselves called themselves the Forces of the Yugoslav People's Army. And there was another title, another name that was repeated often, and that was the Chetniks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware of the term "VRS"?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: I became aware of that term later on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did the acronym VRS stand for?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: I assume the army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. Taric, when the war began, what was your occupation?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: I'm a teacher.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any children?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us the gender and age of your child or children?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: I have a daughter. She is now 17.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What year was she born in?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did there come a time during the war in Sarajevo that both you and your daughter were shot by a sniper?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall the date of this incident?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please tell the Trial Chamber that date.

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: The 3rd of September, 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall the weather on that day?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: It was a warm September day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the sun shining, was it raining, was it cloudy or overcast? Do you recall?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: It was a sunny September day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall approximately what time of the day both you and your daughter were shot?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: About 1700 hours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were you doing at the time that the two of you were shot?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: The school year was about to start, and my daughter was to begin third form. You couldn't buy any textbooks at that time, so I went out to get some textbooks from an older pupil, textbooks that my daughter could use.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was your daughter accompanying you when you went to get these textbooks?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you leave your apartment or your place of residence to go get these textbooks? Is that where you started your journey from?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: Yes. I left from my apartment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And on which side of the front lines was your apartment located?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: On two sides of the front line, actually.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you elaborate, please?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: Could you tell me what you want me to describe?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You testified a moment ago that your apartment was located on two sides of the front line. What did you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: Yes. From two directions. That is to say, there were two danger points from the confrontation lines. Looking at my apartment, there were two points that were vulnerable from the confrontation line.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what those two points were?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: Grbavica and Vrace.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall the route that you took with your daughter on 3 September 1993 to go and collect the textbooks?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please tell the Trial Chamber the route you took.

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: I left my apartment and went through the neighbourhood, below the building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall which streets you were on?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: The street is now called Azize Sacirbegovic Street, but the name before was Ivana Krndelja Street.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. Taric, do you remember giving a statement to an investigator of the Tribunal in November 1995?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember as part of that interview the investigator providing you with a photocopy of a map?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember making certain markings on that map with a pen and a yellow highlighter pen?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, I would ask that the witness be shown the document marked P3105.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, would you please give the document to the witness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. Taric, after you've looked at that document, does that refresh your memory as to the document that you marked for the investigator?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: With the assistance of the usher, I'd ask that that document be placed on the ELMO machine, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. Taric, if you could, please, use the pointer and indicate the direction that you were walking with your daughter on the day that the two of you were shot.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mrs. Taric, would you please do it on the ELMO machine, which is on your right, so that we -- and not on the screen. Mr. Usher, could you please help.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can get up?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. I think it's better to sit down, if possible.

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: This is Hrasno, this is Trg Heroja Street, or square, and this route goes down Ivana Krndelja Street and the place where I was hit by a sniper bullet.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. Taric, does the "X" in the middle of the yellow line that you've drawn indicate the location where you and your daughter were shot?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I notice that the line continues towards the left-hand side of the map, the yellow line. What does that continuation indicate?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: The continuation indicates where we were helped, where my daughter and I were given assistance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you actually walk the full distance of the yellow line as indicated on P3105?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: More or less, yes, the whole line.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. Taric, can you please describe for the Trial Chamber the intersection that you were at at the time you were shot?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: Could you tell me what you mean by that? I'm not quite clear.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall the physical characteristics of the intersection?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: The only part that was open, that was open space, was this intersection. All the other parts of the route were either apartment buildings or protection containers that had been set up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall if there were any protection containers at the intersection where you were shot?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: At the intersection itself, there was no protection. It was an open space.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please describe for us what you heard as you approached that intersection, if anything?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: Unfortunately, I heard nothing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know if there was a ceasefire in existence on that day?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: It was quite a quiet day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please describe for us what happened as you crossed that street?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: As I said, this is the only open space that I had to cross with my daughter, and as soon as we appeared by one of the protection containers, I felt a blunt blow, a blunt blow, and I found myself on the ground from the impact of that. I pulled my daughter with me. We both lay down. I pulled her down.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you -- were you struck by the bullet?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: Yes. The bullet hit me, and because of that, because of this strong hit, I had to lie down on the ground.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In what part of your body did the bullet strike you?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: In the upper part of my leg.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your left leg or your right leg?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: My left leg.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did the bullet go after it struck you?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: I don't know. All I know is that after some time, the bullet, when it passed through my leg, also passed through my daughter's stomach and her hand, and it was probably -- probably ended up on the ground.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall hearing one shot at the time you were struck or more than one shot?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: While we were lying down like that, we heard probably one more bullet which whizzed past our bodies as we lay there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand that, Mrs. Taric. I'm asking you at the time you were hit if you recall hearing more than one shot.

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: I just heard one. Whether there was another one, I don't remember because I was in a state which -- in which I couldn't feel anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. Taric, do you recall what you were wearing that day?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: As it was a warm day, I was wearing jeans and I had a white T-shirt and a denim waistcoat. A white T-shirt and jeans jacket or waistcoat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you wearing any type of clothing that could be characterised as a military uniform?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: Jeans, blue jeans and a blue jeans waistcoat. I don't think that is a uniform of any kind.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you carrying any type of military weapon at the time you were shot?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: No. I was just walking along with my daughter, holding her by the hand.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was your daughter wearing that date?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: She was wearing a red tracksuit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any soldiers or people in military uniforms in the immediate vicinity of you when you were shot?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there any military equipment or heavy military weaponry in the immediate vicinity of the area when you were shot?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall approximately how long you and your daughter remained on the street after being shot?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: Well, barely ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember seeing any other people in the immediate vicinity as you were lying on the street?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: This was the neighbourhood area and there were buildings, and the weather was warm. People were sitting outside in front of their buildings. They were sitting in front of their front doors.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anyone -- immediately after you were shot, did anyone offer to render you and your daughter any type of assistance?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: All of them wanted to help us, but because of the danger, nobody dared go up to the spot that we were at.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did someone eventually come to your assistance?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: I tried to take my daughter to these people. As we were lying down, in this lying-down position, we tried to crawl, and we - I crawled too - and we managed to reach those people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What type of assistance did those people render to you and your Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. daughter?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: A man lifted up my daughter into his arms and carried her all the way, and another man took hold of me under my arm, and that's how we went.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you go?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: We went to the first infirmary.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you and/or your daughter admitted into a hospital?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: After the infirmary, as it was very difficult to find transport to take you to hospital, we managed somehow, though, and managed to reach the hospital.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did you remain in the hospital?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: Twelve days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did your daughter remain in the hospital?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: As long as I did, 12 days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were discharged from the hospital, did the doctor or hospital staff provide you with any type of paperwork?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: Yes. A discharge sheet, the date we were admitted, and the date we left the hospital, and it also says on this piece of paper the injury. It states the injury for which we were treated.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, I would ask that the witness be shown P3369.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Usher, would you please give the exhibit. But I see, Madam Registrar, you're checking on whether this has been ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This document has previously been admitted into evidence, P3369.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I see, Mr. Mundis, that it is marked -- prenumbered P3369A. Is there any difference with the document that has been tendered and admitted into evidence P3369?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: No, Mr. President. The reason the "A" was added is that our trial support assistant placed that on because the document had been previously admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So now we'll show the original to the witness and we have the copies available to us. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. Taric, I would like you to take a look at P3369, the document that's in front of you. Do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: Yes. This is exactly this letter of discharge, and the time that we arrived, and the time that we left the hospital, that we were discharged.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To what person or persons is this document in reference to?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: I was given also a document referring to my daughter Elma.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does the document that's before you refer to your daughter or to yourself?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: To my daughter, Elma.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Might I ask at this time, Mr. President, that the witness be shown the video, which is P3280I.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please. If the technical staff could play the video.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: "THE INVESTIGATOR: Could you please stand at the place where, to the best of your recollection, the edge of the barricade was located on the day that you were shot. NAFA TARIC: [Indicates] THE INVESTIGATOR: I will mark this location with yellow spray paint. Can you please indicate with your hand which area from this location was open. NAFA TARIC: [indicates] THE INVESTIGATOR: Could you please now stand at the spot where, to the best of your recollection, you were when you were wounded. NAFA TARIC: [Indicates] THE INVESTIGATOR: I will now mark the spot, with yellow spray paint, the figure "X," with the number "1" beside it. Would you please show me, to the best of your recollection, where your daughter was located when she was shot. NAFA TARIC: [Indicates] THE INVESTIGATOR: I will now place another "X" with the number "2" at this location. Can you please indicate where, to the best of your recollection, you were when you heard a second shot. NAFA TARIC: [Indicates] THE INVESTIGATOR: Could you please point in the direction from which you heard the sound of the second shot, to the best of your recollection.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Complies] THE INVESTIGATOR: Thank you. Finally, can you please walk in the direction that you and your daughter [indicated] and stop when you reach the location where it was safe, to the best of your recollection.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Complies]"

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. Taric, did you recognise yourself in that videotape?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you comply with the instructions of the investigator to the best of your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you complied with those directions truthfully?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, I would ask that the witness be shown Exhibit P3268, which composes two photographs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please, Mr. Usher, would you give the photographs to the witness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. Taric, I'd ask that you look first at the document with the number 02114324. Have you ever seen this photograph before, Mrs. Taric?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this photograph shown to you by an investigator at the Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you make some markings on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell the Trial Chamber what this photograph depicts?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: Exactly this open space which was protected by containers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With the assistance of the usher, if you could place that photograph on the ELMO machine, please. I draw your attention to the markings in a thick marker in the lower part of the middle of the photograph. Did you make those markings on this document, Mrs. Taric?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do those markings indicate?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: The markings I made was an attempt to try to depict this -- the height of the protection of the protective containers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the day in question, on which side of the containers, these protective barriers, were you and your daughter walking, on the side where the photographer is located or on the side where the automobile which is driving away from the photographer is located?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: We were walking -- as we were crossing the street, it is this side that we were walking.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let the record reflect, Mr. President, that the witness is pointing to the side of the drawings that would be the side that the photographer is located on. Now, Mrs. Taric, which direction, as shown on this photograph, were you and your daughter walking on that day, from left to right or from right to left?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: So we were walking from left to right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in this photograph that is in front of you, can you please point to the approximate location where you and your daughter were walking at the time you were shot?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: The spot would be approximately here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: If the usher could please provide a blue marker to the witness, I would ask that she mark an "X" on the location where she was shot.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mrs. Taric. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. Taric, does this photograph, 02114324, show the area where you heard the second bullet coming from?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please mark that area with the blue pen, perhaps circling the area where you heard the second gunshot come from, please?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you whether you want me to put in the location or the direction.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would ask if you could please circle the location or the area from which you heard the second gunshot. If you could just place a circle around that area or areas, please.

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge or idea where the person who was actually shooting you was located?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: After the incident, we found out that the bullet had come from the other side, from the top of the hill, and the street in question is Ozrenska Street.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you see the approximate location on this photograph of where Ozrenska Street is located?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: The area is -- was going approximately along this street, and it goes up there to the neighbourhood where all these private houses or family houses are, and this is where that street is. So it would be top of the hill.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please again take the blue marker and draw a circle or an oval in the area where you learned that this shot came from.

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: For the record, the second circle which the witness has drawn is immediately above the ridge in --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I ask to have the question asked a little more loudly, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think, Mrs. Taric, that Mr. Mundis was now, just for the record, describing where you put the circle. So this is not a new question, but it just indicates so that we will be able to read later on where actually you marked the photograph. So this is not a new question. It was just indicating where you marked the photograph. So if you please let Mr. Mundis proceed, and when there is a new question, he'll indicate this to you. Yes. Please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. For the record, the second circle which the witness has drawn is immediately above the ridge shown in the photograph, approximately midway through the photograph, halfway through the photograph, and slightly to the right of the centre of the photograph.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. Taric, returning now to the first circle that you drew, that is, the one that is closest to the "X" which you drew, could you please draw a straight line with an arrow on it from that circle towards the direction that you were walking when you were shot.

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. Taric, can you please draw an arrow in the direction from which you heard the second gunshot.

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please place the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I'm sorry, but with these technical difficulties, we now see on our screens a very bad picture. I cannot see a circle or anything whatsoever. We have a very dark image on our screen. We cannot see what the witness is marking.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar just informs me that she has already spoken with the technical booth. So it might be difficult to see it on the screen, but if you're in any need, as soon as the marking has ended, I'll give you the opportunity to inspect specifically the markings before cross-examining the witness, so that you can see on the original photograph what the markings are. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Please proceed, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. Taric, can you please indicate the arrow pointing in the direction you were walking by placing the number "1" next to the arrow.

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: You mean the arrow after I was hit? Do I have to mark that arrow with number "1"?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me try this again, Mrs. Taric. You've marked two arrows on the photograph; is that correct? There's an arrow pointing away from the "X," pointing towards the edge of the photograph. That is the first arrow that you drew. Do you see that arrow?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please place the number "1" by that arrow.

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And just so the record is clear, ma'am, if you could please tell us what that arrow represents.

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: This arrow marked with "1" represents the direction of our movement from the spot where we were wounded, towards the location where we were given first aid.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the second arrow, Mrs. Taric, could you please mark that with the number "2."

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And again, for the record, can you please describe what that arrow represents.

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: The arrow marked with "2" represents the direction from which I heard the following shots, the shots that followed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And by "the shots that followed," you mean the shots that followed after you and your daughter were shot by the bullet; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: With the assistance of the usher, I'd ask that the second photograph of that exhibit, that is, the document marked 02114325, be placed on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. So that we could at least follow this, because now we would like to have a look at this photograph and examine it, the one that was marked by the witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, would you please -- Could the first one already be given to the Defence so they can better follow?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, could you please give this photograph to the Defence so that they can inspect the markings put on the photograph. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, could Mr. Mundis proceed now or ...?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes, certainly, since I believe that we are finished with it very soon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. Taric, I'd ask you now to look at the photo which is on the machine to your right, with the number 02114325 in the lower left corner. Do you recognise this photograph?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you also make some markings on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What markings did you make on the photograph, please?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: I marked the location which was protected by the containers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And would that be the area in the middle of the photograph with the square and the rectangle and hash marks through those, or striped lines through those diagrams?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you also see in this photograph the approximate location where you and your daughter were walking at the time that you were wounded?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Again, Mrs. Taric, I'd ask you to take the blue marker and place an "X" on the location where you and your daughter were at the time you were shot.

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The usher can take that photograph and show it to the Defence counsel. We're finished with it at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Usher, you can take the photograph to the Defence table. I beg your pardon? You don't need it. Okay. Then please return it to the registrar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. Taric, you testified a few moments ago that the location of the person who shot you was on the Ozrenska Street. Do you know on which side of the front lines that street was located at the time you and your daughter were shot?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: I did not understand the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You testified a few moments ago that you subsequently learned that the location of the person who shot you was on the Ozrenska Street; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know which military force controlled the area along the Ozrenska Street on the day that you and your daughter were shot?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: This was -- these were the positions of the forces that attacked Bosnia-Herzegovina. This was the JNA, Yugoslav People's Army, helped by other formations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know, at the time when you and your daughter were shot, whether the VRS was yet in existence and operating under that name?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: I heard about that name much later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To the best of your knowledge, was the VRS a successor to the JNA?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: It probably was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, I note the time. The next area and final area of the direct examination involves the 360-degree photograph, and I don't believe I can --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: How much time do you think it will take? If it's just a matter of, well, let's say ten to seven or eight minutes, we might ask the technical staff or the interpreters' booth whether we could finish the examination-in-chief. Have you any indication?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I would say no more than ten minutes perhaps. More likely closer to five.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would it be any problem both from the courtroom facilities and the assistance of the technical and interpreter staff?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: No problem, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So then I would suggest that you continue. Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I believe that I'm seeing, but perhaps I am maybe making a mistake, and I think that the transcript -- the court reporters are very tired. So of course we can continue as long as necessary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I may not have noticed exactly who else could -- is there any objection? We'll stop immediately. I see no objection from whatever side. Thank you very much for your cooperation. Please proceed then, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I would ask that the 360-degree photograph be shown to the witness now, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, can you please briefly describe what you see in the photograph immediately in front of you on the screen?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: One can see the direction or, rather, the place, these buildings, showing how we arrived, the street that was shielded, and the area where my daughter and I were wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can the photograph please be panned to the right. Stop, please. Can the photograph please be zoomed in. A little bit further, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, in the background of the photograph there appears to be a ridge. Do you know what area is depicted in the photograph in front of you slightly to the left of the centre, to the left of the tree in the centre of the photograph?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: No, I don't know what that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can the photograph please be panned to the right. Stop, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. Taric, do you recognise what is now visible on the screen in front of you?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: I do, yes. That is the road, the route which I covered with my daughter, with my wounded daughter, to then take cover behind this building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would it be correct that there is an area towards the right-hand side of the photo on the bottom where there appears to be a path through the grass? Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that the path that you and your daughter went along after you were being shot?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And to the left of that path there appears to be an area of concrete or asphalt; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that where your daughter and you first received the assistance of people who were standing in the vicinity after being shot?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can the photograph please be panned further to the right. That's fine. Stop.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. Taric, do you see anywhere in the photograph on the screen in front of you the location or direction from which you heard the second gunshot after you and your daughter were wounded?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please describe for us in words the area or areas where you heard that gunshot coming from?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: Well, I heard the shot as coming from my left, and then along the street to the place where I was wounded, the whole length on the left-hand side towards the hill.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And as you were walking, would the path that is in the right-hand side of the photograph, extending into the distance, would that have been on your left at the time you were shot?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To the best of your knowledge then, did the shot come from somewhere along the ridge at the back of -- towards the rear and in the middle of the photograph on the screen in front of you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand the question, where were the bullets coming or, rather, whether the bullets came from such-and-such place, because this sounds a leading question. That is at least what I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you please rephrase your question, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. Taric, on the photograph shown in front of you on the screen, do you -- can you indicate to us from where you heard the second gunshot? That would be the shot after you and your daughter were wounded.

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: As I was moving, as I was walking down the left-hand side, from that side, that is from my left side, I heard a shot covering -- coming from across the whole of the open space towards the hill.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, I did neglect to ask the witness one question or a series of -- a couple of questions with respect to the second photograph that she was shown a few moments ago.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could it be done in just a couple of minutes? Because otherwise --

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed then.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I'd ask that she be shown the photograph marked 02114325.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. I'm sorry, but for the transcript it is important I note that in the transcript in English there are certain things which I say which are not interpreted. Therefore, we shall have to find some solution for this problem, because if you follow the English transcript and if I'm trying to say something, then I think that for better or for worse, everything that Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. I have said should be interpreted. Thank you very much in advance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Was this about the objection you made against the questioning?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, indeed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... for the -- for the final version of the -- of the transcript. You know that overnight they're still working on it. If there would remain any part untranslated by tomorrow, please write down precisely which part it is and give it to us so that we can take care that proper attention will be paid to it. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I ask that that photograph be placed on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. Taric, to the right-hand side of that photograph there is a rather tall building that appears to be a block of flats with a white side towards the photograph. If you look then immediately to the left where you've drawn the two diagrams indicating the containers. Do you see that on the photograph?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: I do, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And between the diagram and the building, there is what appears to be a small grassy area.

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you -- did you and your daughter pass through that area, through that general area at the time or shortly before you were shot?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall on the day that the two of you were shot whether or not that area was open or was there a container in that location where the grass is shown between the diagram and the building?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: Yes. The area where you see grass now, about half of this current grass patch was protected.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was part of that area also then open? If part of it was protected, it would follow that part of it was open. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC
utterances.text: Well, most of it. The part which follows the grass patch, and that is the pedestrian path, that was open, fully open, the only thing that was open.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Thank you very much, Mrs. Taric. The Prosecution has no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mrs. Taric, we will have a break now until tomorrow at 9.00. We'll then continue. I hope you were not too nervous, because it's quite a new environment for you, I think, a courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I am slightly upset, of course, and talking about things that happened so many years ago, now to remember it all, after all this time, it does have its effect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We hope that, as far as possible in these circumstances, you feel comfortable, and we'll then see you back tomorrow morning at 9.00. We'll adjourn until Wednesday, 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 6th day of February 2002, at 9.00 a.m.
